construct.diagnosis_or_process: Dominant-negative THRA variants cause resistance to thyroid hormone alpha, producing hypothyroid features in TRα-predominant tissues such as bone and gastrointestinal tract with low-normal T4, high-normal T3, low T4/T3 ratio, and relatively preserved TSH feedback.

source_verification.title: Resistance to thyroid hormone mediated by defective thyroid hormone receptor alpha
Thyroid hormone resistance syndrome due to mutations in the thyroid hormone receptor α gene (THRA)

second_answer_attack.resolution: THRB-mediated resistance generally produces elevated circulating thyroid hormones with nonsuppressed TSH and often goiter. The low-normal T4, high-normal T3, low T4/T3 ratio, constipation and skeletal phenotype with preserved TSH feedback are characteristic of resistance to thyroid hormone alpha.

blind_audit.rationale: TRα1 is prominent in bone, gastrointestinal tract, heart, and other tissues. Dominant-negative THRA variants can therefore cause growth retardation, skeletal dysplasia/delayed bone age, constipation, and bradycardia while the pituitary-thyroid axis is much less perturbed than in THRB-mediated resistance; low-normal T4 and high-normal T3 are characteristic clues. Strongest alternative resolved: THRB-mediated resistance generally produces elevated circulating thyroid hormones with nonsuppressed TSH and often goiter. The low-normal T4, high-normal T3, low T4/T3 ratio, constipation and skeletal phenotype with preserved TSH feedback are characteristic of resistance to thyroid hormone alpha.
